title: Number of 1 Bits
statement: Return the number of 1 bits in the binary representation of the non-negative integer `n`. This is the Hamming weight.
hints: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
Repeat until n is 0 and count the operations.
The loop runs once per set bit, not once per bit position.

approaches.name: Shift and test
approaches.explanation: Test the low bit and shift.

approaches.name: Kernighan
approaches.explanation: Clear the lowest set bit each iteration.

editorial: Subtracting one flips every bit up to and including the lowest 1. AND-ing with the original number clears that 1 and leaves the higher bits unchanged. Counting those clears is the popcount.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def hamming_weight(n: int) -> int:
    count = 0
    while n:
        n &= n - 1
        count += 1
    return count
